To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have identified the conserved and regulatory role of either 5' or 3' U rich region of a subset of mRNA species in female gametocyte of Plasmodium falciparum.
the 3' and 5' UTRLs play conserved roles in TR and are essential for the regulation of translation in P. berghei female gametocytes.

the conserved and sexually specific regulatory role of the 5' and 3' U TR of a subset of TR associated mRNA species was shown by almost complete repression of expression of a reporter protein in the gametocytes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a conserved and essential RNA element that plays an important role during development of female gametes in the human malaria parasite.
the regulation of gene expression in Plasmodia.
the identification of a novel and conserved U rich element in the 5'- and 3'-UTR of translationally repressible mRNAs in Plasmodum falciparum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TR is a conserved and sex dependent phenomenon in Plasmodia.
the conserved U rich element identified here in the 3'/5' UTRs of TR associated transcripts is a key player in mediating TR of the mRNA in female gametocyte.

a conserved U rich TR element in either the 3 or 5' untranslated regions of TR associated transcripts is essential for TR and that this TR element is located in the 5 or 3' untranslated region of TR associated transcripts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that the conserved U rich TR associated element in the 3’ UTR and a similar element in the 5’ UTR play an essential role in the regulation of translation in the female gametes of Plasmodium falciparum and Plasmodium berghei.
we have identified a U rich RNA region that is involved in TR and is conserved between 5' and 3' U TR of TR associated genes in Plasmodia.
we have identified a conserved U rich element in the 5 UTR of TR mRNAs that can mediate translational repression in the gametocytes of P. berghei.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 3' and 5' U rich RNA elements identified in this study can act in cis and are conserved across species.
the 3' and 5' UTS of the TR-associated transcripts play an important role in the regulation of translation of a subset of mRNA species in the female gametes of P. berghei.
the UTR of TR transcripts plays an important role during the early stages of development of Plasmodium gametocytes.
